18.60000,60.10000.name: Field trial with genetically modified aspen and hybrid aspen dnr 4.6.18-14 201/17
18.60000,60.10000.type: organism not named in the title, national biosafety decision
18.60000,60.10000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-121.51600,38.61230.name: California IVF Fertility Center
-121.51600,38.61230.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Ernest J. Zeringue, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-97.33750,37.69220.name: The Center for Reproductive Medicine
-97.33750,37.69220.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: David Grainger, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-86.14337,39.70772.name: Planned Parenthood
-86.14337,39.70772.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. Operated by Planned Parenthood. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

5.28959,45.83060.name: Centre de Recherche de Saint Vulbas
5.28959,45.83060.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health France. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-78.61458,-0.93403.name: Provida Nacer ReproducciÃ³n Humana
-78.61458,-0.93403.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://providanacer.com. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

-88.02138,43.04358.name: Center for Infectious Disease Research (CIDR)
-88.02138,43.04358.state: TBRC, 3rd Floor 8701 Watertown Plank Rd. Milwaukee, WI 53226, United States
-88.02138,43.04358.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Medical College of Wisconsin. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on both human and animal health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

30.52340,50.45010.name: Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food (Ukraine)
30.52340,50.45010.desc: Ukraine has no functioning approval system for engineered crops and substantial evidence they are grown anyway, unregistered, on a large share of soy and maize area. A country with no register does not thereby have no engineered crops; it has no record of them, and the war has made the gap wider.

30.52340,50.45010.name: BioTexCom
30.52340,50.45010.desc: Ukraine became one of the few countries offering commercial surrogacy to foreigners with legal clarity on parentage from birth, and fourteen companies were operating there before the war. The largest reported awaiting around 500 births at one point; surrogates were paid in the region of fifteen to seventeen thousand dollars. The country keeps no national statistics on surrogacy, which is itself the finding — a sector large enough to lead the world in births for foreign parents, with no register of how many. Two events showed what the arrangement rests on. In 2020 border closures left at least a hundred newborns in clinic care awaiting parents from twelve countries, with officials warning the figure could reach a thousand. In 2022 the invasion left surrogates displaced and parents unable to reach the country; one clinic reported 140 surrogates more than twelve weeks pregnant. Members of parliament have since proposed suspending the service for foreigners, while clinics argue for regulation instead of a ban.

36.77000,-1.32000.name: Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service
36.77000,-1.32000.desc: Kenya's plant health and seed regulator, responsible for variety approval and seed certification, and the body that had to implement the 2022 lifting of the engineered-crop import ban while a court challenge to that decision was still running. Regulators in this position carry out a policy that may be reversed above them.
